title: CouchDB Mango Query Language
mediaType: None known — Mango selectors are POSTed as a JSON document to `/db/_find` using the generic `application/json` media type.

expressiveness.rationale: JSON-based selector syntax supports rich operators ($gt, $lt, $in, $regex, etc.), sorting, field projection, pagination via bookmarks, and execution-stats/explain introspection, but lacks SQL-style joins or aggregation.

simplicity.rationale: Declarative JSON selector documents are straightforward to construct without writing JavaScript map/reduce views; Mango was created specifically to simplify CouchDB querying.

flexibility.rationale: Operates over CouchDB's schema-less JSON documents and can create ad hoc indexes on the fly, well suited to evolving document shapes.

communityAndEcosystem.rationale: Backed by the Apache Software Foundation with solid documentation, but CouchDB has a smaller, more specialized community (offline-first/sync use cases) than mainstream NoSQL databases.

extensibility.rationale: Selector operators and index types (json/text/nouveau) are fixed by CouchDB; Mango itself provides no user-defined functions, unlike the older JavaScript map/reduce views.

transportCompatibility.rationale: Mango queries are POSTed as JSON bodies to CouchDB's native HTTP _find endpoint, making the language inherently designed for HTTP-based access, consistent with CouchDB's all-HTTP API design.

standardization.rationale: A CouchDB/Mango-specific syntax with no independent standard or cross-vendor adoption.

security.rationale: Being JSON-document based rather than a string-concatenated query language reduces classic injection risk, though care is still needed with dynamically constructed selectors.

performance.rationale: Relies on explicit or automatically-selected secondary indexes; querying without a suitable index falls back to the slow built-in _all_docs index, which the docs explicitly warn against.

orthogonality.rationale: Selector, sort, fields, and pagination options compose predictably as JSON, though sort fields must already be covered by an existing index, a documented constraint on composability.

summary: CouchDB's Mango query language offers a simple, JSON-native declarative alternative to hand-written map/reduce views, well suited to CouchDB's HTTP-first, schema-less document model, but it is CouchDB-specific with no independent standardization and lacks SQL-style joins or aggregation.

example.scenario: Retrieve products where category = "electronics" and price > 100, sorted by price descending, page 2 of 10 per page.
example.notes: skip/limit are native, documented fields, though Mango's own docs recommend the response bookmark for continued paging over large skip values.
